subject: Private deployment preflight — VPC peering, private endpoints & on-prem packaging
messages:
From: Suresh Gupta <suresh.gupta@lumenforge.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: network-team@lumenforge.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: LumenForge private deployment — preflight items and kickoff

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're preparing for a Private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoints) and want to run a short preflight so we can validate network, DNS, and on-prem packaging constraints before the formal kickoff. Can your team review the attached high-level networking notes and tell us what specific CIDR ranges, port ranges, and FQDN patterns Redwood needs? Also: we plan to run the on-prem package in an air-gapped staging cluster first — any special requirements around image signing or package transfer you recommend?

Attached: rfp-networking-notes.pdf

Ideally we'd align on a checklist and get a 45m call next week. Proposed times: Mon/Tue morning PST.

Thanks,
Suresh
Suresh Gupta
Head of Infrastructure, LumenForge Systems
ops: +1 415-555-0147

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Suresh Gupta <suresh.gupta@lumenforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenForge private deployment — preflight items and kickoff

Hi Suresh — thanks for the note and the attachment. We're excited to get this moving. Quick summary of what we'll cover in the preflight and the high-level asks from our side: 

- Required network items: preferred VPC peer CIDRs (we recommend non-overlapping /16 or /20 blocks), a list of application and management CIDRs, and your NAT/egress IPs for allowlisting.
- Ports: primary service 443 (TLS) for private endpoints; ephemeral ranges for health checks and KV sync (we usually recommend 32768-61000 for ephemeral, but can restrict on request).
- DNS: private FQDN pattern (we create redwood-internal.<customer>.svc.<region> for endpoint SRV records) — we need zone delegation or conditional forwarders for the private zone.
- On-prem package: we support a signed tarball and an install manifest (attached draft: onprem-manifest-v0.3.xlsx). For air-gapped installs we provide signed artifacts plus an MD5/SHA256 checksum file and an install bootstrap script; transfer via your secure media is fine.

Irene will follow up with KMS/HSM requirements and the minimal connectivity matrix we need to validate the KV cache and telemetry (we keep telemetry optional for first cut).

Propose 45m call Monday 11/16 at 10:00am PST. Does that work?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: onprem-manifest-v0.3.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Suresh Gupta <suresh.gupta@lumenforge.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenForge private deployment — preflight items and kickoff

Thanks Suresh / Mateo. A few technical clarifications from security/ops side before the call: 

1) KMS/HSM: If you plan to use customer-managed keys, please confirm which KMS provider (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, vault.myorg) and whether the key usage policy allows signing of auth tokens. For HSM-attached keys we'll need to validate PKCS#11 compatibility.
2) Private endpoint naming: confirm whether you prefer explicit hostnames per environment (prod/redwood) or wildcard delegation. We prefer explicit names for easier tracing in logs.
3) Egress & telemetry: you can opt out of telemetry; if enabled, we require a single egress allowlist to us (ips.redwood.com) and a TLS inspection exception if you do MITM for outbound.
4) Health checks: we rely on short-lived ephemeral connections from our monitoring agents; if you have strict network ACLs, set 10s-60s timeouts on LB health checks.

Also — for the on-prem package transfer, please provide the PGP public key you intend to use for signing the transfer bundle (we'll sign the manifest and verify on install).

Irene Choi
Security & Integrations | Redwood Inference

Thanks — confirm Monday 11/16 10:00am PST works for the team. A couple of items ahead of the call: 

- Our net team attached the CIDR plan and egress list here: netplan_v2.xlsx (I'll share on the call). Tentatively we will use 10.44.0.0/16 for the infra VPC and 10.88.0.0/16 for the app VPC.
- For on-prem transfer we plan to use a secure media jumpbox (signed by our internal PKI) and we'll provide a PGP key.
- Question: can Redwood operate with ephemeral ports restricted to a narrower range (we'd prefer 49152-49999) for compliance reasons?

I'll upload the netplan and PGP key to the Drive link you shared prior to the call.

Suresh

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: LumenForge private deployment — preflight items and kickoff

Great — thanks Suresh. Short answers and next steps: 

- Ephemeral ports: we can support 49152-49999 but will need to run a short soak in staging to verify KV sync performance (may increase tail latency slightly). We'll document any observed regressions in the runbook.
- CIDRs you listed (10.44/16 and 10.88/16) are fine — please confirm there are no overlapping peering routes with other partners.
- On-prem transfer: PGP-signed bundle + checksum is perfect. We'll verify signatures during install and provide a verification script.

Action items for the call (Monday 11/16 10:00am PST):
1) LumenForge: upload netplan_v2.xlsx and PGP public key to the Drive link
2) Redwood: run the stage soak with ephemeral range and surface any perf notes (Irene to own telemetry/allowlist ask)
3) Agree on DNS delegation approach and pre-create conditional forwarders if needed

I've added the runbook link for the call and appended the meeting invite for 10:00-10:45 PST. Look forward to it.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
